```markdown
# Tasks

## 1. Project scaffolding and health endpoint

- [ ] 1.1 Create `requirements.txt` (fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy>=2, psycopg[binary], pydantic, pydantic-settings, pyjwt, argon2-cffi), `requirements-dev.txt` (pytest, httpx) and `pytest.ini` with `testpaths = tests`; verify both requirement files install cleanly with `pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt` and that `pytest --collect-only` exits without error
- [ ] 1.2 Create `app/__init__.py`, `app/config.py` (settings read from the environment: `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES`), `app/database.py` (engine, session factory, `Base`) and `app/models.py` (tables `users` with unique `email`, `hashed_password` and `role`; `pets` with `name`, `species`, `birth_date` and `owner_id`; `appointments` with `pet_id`, `vet_id`, `start_at`, `end_at` and `status`, plus the `UtcDateTime` decorator); verify by importing `app.models` and running `Base.metadata.create_all` against an in-memory SQLite engine
- [ ] 1.3 Create `app/schemas.py` with the request and response models of the health and identity endpoints, `app/main.py` (FastAPI application, router mounting, `create_all` on startup) and `app/routers/__init__.py` plus `app/routers/health.py` serving `GET /health`; verify that a request to `GET /health` answers HTTP 200 with the body `{"status": "ok"}`
- [ ] 1.4 Create `tests/__init__.py`, `tests/conftest.py` (application fixture bound to an in-memory SQLite database, per-test table cleanup, helpers to register a user, to log in and to build an `Authorization: Bearer` header) and `tests/test_health.py`; verify `pytest tests/test_health.py` passes and that the suite covers the public health response and its exact JSON body

## 2. Authentication, roles and bearer protection

- [ ] 2.1 Create `app/security.py` (password hashing with argon2, JWT issuing and verification with PyJWT, carrying the user id, the role and an expiry) and `app/dependencies.py` (`get_current_user` raising 401 for a missing, malformed or invalid token, `require_client` raising 403 for a veterinarian); verify with `tests/test_auth.py` that a freshly issued token is accepted by the dependency and that a token signed with another key is rejected
- [ ] 2.2 Implement `POST /auth/register` in `app/routers/auth.py` returning HTTP 201 with `{id, email, role}`, HTTP 422 for a role outside `client`/`vet` and for a password shorter than 8 characters, and HTTP 409 for an email that is already registered; verify with `tests/test_auth.py` covering each status code and that the response body never contains the password
- [ ] 2.3 Implement `POST /auth/login` returning HTTP 200 with `{access_token, token_type: "bearer"}` for valid credentials and HTTP 401 for a wrong password and for an unknown email; verify with `tests/test_auth.py` asserting the token is a JWT and that the stored credential is not the plaintext password
- [ ] 2.4 Register the `users` role on every account creation path so that a veterinarian is stored with role `vet` and a client with role `client`; verify with `tests/test_auth.py` that a registered veterinarian can log in and that the issued token resolves to that account

## 3. Veterinarian directory and pet registry

- [ ] 3.1 Implement `GET /vets` in `app/routers/vets.py` returning HTTP 200 with an array of `{id, email}` for the accounts whose role is `vet`; verify with `tests/test_vets.py` that the listing holds only veterinarians and that it answers HTTP 401 without a bearer token
- [ ] 3.2 Implement `POST /pets` and `GET /pets` in `app/routers/pets.py`: HTTP 201 with `{id, name, species, birth_date, owner_id}` for a client, HTTP 403 for a veterinarian, HTTP 422 for a species outside `dog`/`cat`/`other` and for a birth date later than today, and a listing restricted to the pets of the authenticated client; verify with `tests/test_pets.py` covering every status code and the owner scoping
- [ ] 3.3 Add the `species` literal and the future `birth_date` rejection to the pet schemas in `app/schemas.py` so that the same rules hold for every client of the registry; verify with `tests/test_pets.py` that a pet born today is accepted and one born tomorrow is refused with HTTP 422

## 4. Appointment scheduling

- [ ] 4.1 Add the appointment request and response schemas to `app/schemas.py` (`pet_id`, `vet_id`, `start_at` in, `{id, pet_id, vet_id, start_at, end_at, status}` out, with `status` limited to `scheduled` and `cancelled`) and the calendar rules helper in `app/routers/appointments.py` that reads `start_at` as UTC and rejects any minute other than `00`/`30`, any leftover second, any weekday outside Monday to Saturday and any start outside 09:00 to 17:30 UTC; verify with `tests/test_appointments.py` that an off-grid minute, a Sunday, an 08:30 start and an 18:00 start each answer HTTP 422
- [ ] 4.2 Implement `POST /appointments` in `app/routers/appointments.py`: HTTP 201 with a 30 minute slot and `status` `scheduled`, HTTP 403 for a veterinarian or for a pet owned by somebody else, HTTP 404 for an unknown pet or an unknown veterinarian, HTTP 422 for a start in the past, and HTTP 409 when the veterinarian already holds that slot; verify with `tests/test_appointments.py` covering each status code and that `end_at` is `start_at` plus 30 minutes
- [ ] 4.3 Implement `GET /appointments` returning HTTP 200 with the appointments of the client's own pets for a client and the appointments where the caller is the veterinarian for a veterinarian; verify with `tests/test_appointments.py` that neither role sees the other's appointments
- [ ] 4.4 Implement `POST /appointments/{id}/cancel` returning HTTP 200 with the appointment whose `status` is `cancelled` for the owning client and for the appointment's veterinarian, HTTP 403 for any other user, HTTP 409 when the appointment was already cancelled and HTTP 404 for an unknown identifier; verify with `tests/test_appointments.py` that the cancelled slot can be booked again with HTTP 201
- [ ] 4.5 Assert the complete protection matrix in `tests/test_auth.py`: `GET /vets`, `POST /pets`, `GET /pets`, `POST /appointments`, `GET /appointments` and `POST /appointments/{id}/cancel` each answer HTTP 401 without a token, with a malformed header and with an invalid token, while `GET /health`, `POST /auth/register` and `POST /auth/login` stay reachable; verify with `pytest tests/test_auth.py` passing

## 5. Container delivery

- [ ] 5.1 Create `Dockerfile` at the repository root on a `python:3.11-slim` base that installs `requirements.txt`, copies `app/` and starts `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`; verify statically that every path the file copies exists in the repository and that no path outside the build context is referenced
- [ ] 5.2 Create `docker-compose.yml` at the repository root with an `api` service built from that `Dockerfile`, a `postgres:16-alpine` service, a named volume for the database data and a `DATABASE_URL` on the API service pointing at the database service; verify statically that the file parses as YAML, that the service names and the `DATABASE_URL` host agree and that the volume is declared
- [ ] 5.3 Create `.dockerignore` (`.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `tests`, local databases) and `.env.example` documenting `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET` and `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES`; verify that every variable the application reads from the environment appears in `.env.example`
- [ ] 5.4 Check that the container files stay consistent with the application: the module path given to uvicorn (`app.main:app`) is importable, the database URL scheme used by the compose file is the one `app/config.py` accepts and the port published by the API service matches the port the container command listens on; verify by reading the three files side by side

## 6. README and end to end verification

- [ ] 6.1 Create `README.md` with how to run the project (local virtual environment with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at PostgreSQL, and the container route with `docker compose up --build`), the environment variables and one curl example per endpoint with its expected status code; verify that each example's method, path, body and status code match an implemented route by listing the application's routes
- [ ] 6.2 Run the complete suite with `pytest -q` and verify that every test of the change passes, that no test needs a Docker daemon and that no test reads the content of `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` or `README.md`

```
